name: LLaVA-OneVision: Easy Visual Task Transfer
problem: Single-image, multi-image and video VLMs were separately built, so capabilities did not transfer between them.
mechanism: Consolidates data, model and visual-representation lessons from the LLaVA-NeXT blog series into one architecture where a single model handles single-image, multi-image and video, with anyres-style visual encoding producing tokens that a single LM consumes.
notes:
Technical report, no peer-reviewed venue found. Relevant to inference because anyres multi-crop encoding is the dominant source of vision-token count in the LLaVA family: each additional tile adds a full patch grid to the LM prefill. It is also one of the most commonly deployed open VLMs in self-hosted serving stacks, so its token behaviour is what most people actually experience.
